title: Raas Leela Brings 130 Performers and Bollywood Spectacle to Austin Long Center
excerpt: A sweeping South Asian musical reimagines a star-crossed love story with nine dance pieces spanning classical, folk, and Bollywood styles at Dell Hall on August 22.
body:
• Raas Leela: An East Side Story, a large-scale Bollywood musical featuring 130 performers and 12 choreographers, premieres at Austin's Long Center on August 22
  • Produced by Agni Foundation for the Arts, the show reimagines a classic star-crossed love story through a South Asian lens with nine dance pieces spanning Bollywood, contemporary, folk, and classical styles
  • Tickets range from $42 to $132 for the Dell Hall performance, one of the largest South Asian theatrical productions staged in Central Texas

A Bollywood Spectacle Comes to Austin

A classic love story is getting a South Asian makeover when Agni Foundation for the Arts and Agni Katha present Raas Leela: An East Side Story at Dell Hall at the Long Center for the Performing Arts in Austin, Texas, on August 22 at 7:30 p.m.

The production features 130 performers, a production team of 20, nine dance pieces, and 12 choreographers drawing on styles that include Bollywood, contemporary, folk, classical, and modern fusion—making it one of the most ambitious South Asian theatrical undertakings Central Texas has seen.

The Story

Set in the fictional city of Vrindapur, the production follows Ram and Leela, two young lovers caught between the powerful, rival Kothari and Rathod families. The narrative draws on the emotional architecture of classic Western love stories—think star-crossed lovers, family rivalry, and generational conflict—reimagined through a distinctly South Asian cultural lens.

\"Raas Leela: An East Side Story is a bold reimagining of a classic narrative, where the heartbeat of South Asian culture meets a universal tale of love and legacy.\"

— Prakash Mohandas, Founder, Agni Foundation for the Arts

Suhaani Srireddy and Arya Santosh take the lead roles, supported by an ensemble that includes Rohit Ramachandran, Mrunmayee Phadke, and Sazu Khadem. The city of Vrindapur itself functions as a character, brought to life by a massive dance ensemble moving between scenes of celebration, chaos, conflict, and memory.

More Than a Love Story

While the star-crossed lovers sit at the heart of the production, the creators describe Raas Leela as a story about community, legacy, pride, and the choices that shape generations. The sweeping staging blends dance, theater, music, and cinematic storytelling into what the production team calls a \"spectacle of movement and emotion.\"

The nine dance pieces span a wide range of South Asian performance traditions. Bollywood numbers anchor the production, but classical Indian dance, folk forms, contemporary movement, and modern fusion each get featured choreography, reflecting the diversity of the South Asian performing arts tradition.

Austin's Growing South Asian Arts Scene

The production is a marker of how Austin's South Asian community has grown large and confident enough to fill Dell Hall—a 2,442-seat venue that typically hosts touring Broadway shows, Austin Symphony Orchestra performances, and major comedy acts. Agni Foundation for the Arts has built a reputation in the Austin area for large-scale cultural events, and this production is their most ambitious yet.

The Long Center bills the event as a venue rental presented by an independent organization, noting that it is committed to providing a safe and welcoming environment for all patrons.

Practical Details

Raas Leela: An East Side Story runs on August 22, 2026, at 7:30 p.m. at Dell Hall, The Long Center for the Performing Arts, 701 W. Riverside Drive, Austin, TX. Tickets range from $42 to $132 and are available at agniartsfoundation.org. The show is expected to run approximately two hours. All patrons, regardless of age, require a ticket to attend.

For South Asian families in the Austin–San Antonio corridor, the show offers a rare chance to see Indian classical, folk, and Bollywood performance traditions staged at professional scale in a major performing arts venue—without traveling to Houston, Dallas, or the coasts.
